change_summary: Promoted a runtime sizing experiment into code: `portfolio_engine.size_signals()` now keeps the caller's normal regime risk for most signals but applies a 0.25 risk multiplier when `trade_quality_score < 0.85`. Added sizing audit fields (`base_risk_pct`, `trade_quality_score`, `tqs_risk_multiplier_applied`) and unit tests for low/high-TQS cases. Re-ran the accepted A+B stack across three non-overlapping windows with the repo venv.

delta_metrics.note: This is the first accepted allocation rule in the current A+B regime-aware-exit stack: it materially improves the primary window, also improves the ripping-bull comparison window, and leaves the weak window unchanged rather than sacrificing it.

hypothesis: If `confidence_score` is now saturated at 1.0 for the accepted A+B stack, the next unblocked allocation-alpha mechanism is to size off richer cross-sectional quality instead of binary entry eligibility. De-risking only lower-`trade_quality_score` signals may improve expected value without reducing trade count, because TQS still differentiates weaker breakout/trend setups even when they all clear the hard gates.
next_retry_requires: If allocation alpha is extended, start from `trade_quality_score` or another richer cross-sectional quality field, not from `confidence_score < 1.0`
Do not re-open global low-confidence sizing; confidence is now saturated on the accepted A+B stack
When revisiting allocation, prefer another context-conditioned marginal-value rule over global slot-count or naive strategy-priority dials
notes: The key new mechanism insight is that allocation alpha was not blocked; the earlier failure was the wrong quality proxy. `trade_quality_score` still carries usable marginal information after the current entry stack has already saturated raw confidence.

low_tqs_definition.new: signals with `trade_quality_score < 0.85` use only 25% of the normal risk budget
low_tqs_definition.old: all passing A+B signals used the same regime risk budget
